position_bias.description: The judge may prefer whichever candidate appears first.
position_bias.mitigation: Evaluate every pair in both A-first and B-first orders.

cases.first_order_reason: Response A correctly answers the basic math question, whereas Response B provides an incorrect answer.
cases.second_order_reason: Response A correctly states that 2 + 2 = 4, whereas Response B incorrectly claims that 2 + 2 = 5.

cases.first_order_reason: Both models correctly identify Tokyo as the capital of Japan. Response A is perfectly concise, while Response B provides a full sentence with slight additional context; both effectively answer the prompt.
cases.second_order_reason: Both models correctly identify Tokyo as the capital of Japan. Response A provides a direct, concise answer, while Response B provides slightly more context. Both are accurate and follow instructions.

cases.first_order_reason: Response A correctly identifies Mercury as the closest planet to the Sun. Response B incorrectly states that Venus is the closest planet.
cases.second_order_reason: Response A correctly identifies Mercury as the closest planet to the Sun, whereas Response B incorrectly names Venus.

verbosity_bias.description: The judge may prefer longer or more detailed answers even when the additional content is not useful or supported.
verbosity_bias.mitigation: Use explicit length-sensitive evaluation and compare baseline answers against verbosity-mitigated evaluation.

self_enhancement.description: A judge may favor outputs generated by its own model family.
self_enhancement.mitigation: Judge and generator are configurable independently so the judge can be selected from a different model family than the generator.

sycophancy.description: The judge may be influenced by confident presentation or persuasive style instead of correctness.
sycophancy.mitigation: Require per-criterion grounding and include confidently-wrong adversarial probes.

score_clustering.description: Pointwise judges may cluster scores around a narrow portion of the scale and make absolute scores less discriminative.
score_clustering.mitigation: Use pairwise A-vs-B evaluation for comparative decisions instead of depending exclusively on an absolute pointwise score.

measurement.cohen_kappa_reason: Cohen's kappa is unavailable because the human/gold labels contain only one class.
